sections.h2: Who assesses and bills property in Rowan County
sections.html:
Rowan County Tax Administration has two divisions, the Assessor's office and the Tax Collector's office. The Assessor lists, assesses and bills all taxable property in the county, and the collector takes payment. Real property appraisers answer at 704-216-8586, and listing questions go to 704-216-8558.

An electronic online listing process is being built and should be ready for the 2027 listing season. Until then, call the office to ask how to list personal property such as a boat, a camper or a mobile home each January.

The Tax Assessor pages link to a land records map tool. A parcel may also carry a municipal or district bill on top of the county bill, so check the tax record for every levy before you list.

Rowan revalues every four years. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, the next is January 1, 2027, and another is set for January 2031.

State law sets only an outer limit of eight years. The shorter cycle softens sticker shock, and a revaluation never sets a rate, because the commissioners set rates in the yearly budget. Values come from actual sales.

Rowan County revaluation timeline
EventDate or result
Last revaluationJanuary 1, 2023
Average real property increase at that revaluation44.96% since the period that ended December 31, 2018
Next revaluationEffective January 1, 2027
Following revaluationScheduled for January 2031

If you sell near a revaluation date, expect buyers to study the new assessed value, because it drives the bill they will inherit. Value follows the condition of a parcel on January 1, so tell the assessor about any building added, moved or torn down.

Real property values rose by an average of 44.96% from the prior period. Almost 12,000 residential and 700 business property sales from January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2022 went into that work.

The county's total taxable base moved from about $14.4 billion to a projected $18.5 billion, with real property revalued to about $15.5 billion. Vehicles, personal property and utilities fell, so the total base rose 28.5% against a 44.96% jump for real estate alone. County law also required a revenue-neutral rate to be reported to the commissioners, who could lower the rate to ease the increase.

A revaluation can reset a buyer's bill sharply even when the rate drops. Check the current assessed value on the county's parcel tools before you set a price, and remember the next reset in 2027.

COMPER is an online tool that shows the valid sales the tax office uses to help set values for the 2027 cycle. Enter a property address and you get a list and a map of valid sales within a five-mile radius, covering January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026.

From that list you can pick sales similar to your home and turn them into a printable or PDF report. The map includes a street view of each comparable property. A seller can use the report to test a listing price against what the assessor treats as valid sales, though it can't replace an agent's or appraiser's opinion.

Call the tax office first, then use the written form if the call doesn't settle it. Informal talks usually happen from January through March. Fill in the Real Property Appeal Form and attach supporting papers. A review can leave the number alone, cut it or raise it.

The formal stage works like this:

  • Real property appeals must arrive before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns for the year.
  • That Board meets for the first time sometime between early April and early May. The county publishes notice in a local paper three times, beginning at least 10 days ahead.
  • Each side gets time to speak. The Board may rule at once or deliberate, and you should receive the ruling in writing.
  • Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which meets monthly in Raleigh and behaves like a trial court. The owner carries the burden of proof, and companies and LLCs need a North Carolina attorney.

Personal property follows a shorter clock of 30 days from the first notice of value. When no separate notice goes out, the bill itself is the notice. After the Board adjourns it may still take up discovered property, classified vehicles, audits and personal property cases.

September 1 is the due date under state law, and no interest accrues until January 6. After that, two percent applies through the end of January, then three-fourths of a percent for each additional month or part of one.

Counties may adopt a prepayment discount by resolution before May 1. Confirm any discount, card fee or payment channel with the Rowan County Tax Collector, since those details are set locally.

Personal property listing takes place in January, and the commissioners may extend it.

Three state programs exist, and each applicant is limited to one. Applications for the elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker programs are due by June 1 of the year of application. Other exemptions are filed in January.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of the first $25,000 or half of appraised value, for owners aged 65 or up or fully and permanently disabled, with 2026 household income no higher than $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to the first $45,000. An unremarried surviving spouse can qualify, and age and income play no role.
  • Circuit breaker: an owner of five years or more with income up to $58,200 may defer tax above 4% of income at or under $38,800, or above 5% in the higher band.

Under the circuit breaker, multiple owners must all qualify, and you reapply each year. The deferred tax is a lien. The most recent three years come due with interest if the owner transfers, dies or stops using the home as a residence. Present-use value applications are filed each January, or after a value change notice.

The sale proceeds cover them. Each year's lien sticks to the parcel from the January listing date, along with interest and costs. A lien for personal property tax can reach all of the owner's real estate inside the taxing unit.

Left unpaid, a bill can lead to a suit and an auction of the parcel. Until the court confirms that sale, the owner can still redeem by clearing the tax and its extras.

Ask the Rowan County Tax Collector for a written payoff on each parcel and hand it to your closing attorney. Do this first if you plan a quick sale, since back taxes shape both price and timing.

faqs.q: When is Rowan County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: The next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, and the following one is scheduled for January 2031 on a four-year cycle.

faqs.q: What is the first move if my Rowan County value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the tax office, since informal reviews usually run January through March. If that fails, send the Real Property Appeal Form with your evidence before the county board adjourns.

faqs.q: What is the deadline on a Rowan County personal property valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the first notice of value. Without a separate notice, the tax bill serves as that notice.
COMPER is the county's online comparison tool. Enter an address to see valid sales from January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026 within five miles, and build a report from similar homes.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Rowan County Tax Assessor?
faqs.a: Real property appraisers are at 704-216-8586, and listing questions go to 704-216-8558. The Tax Assessor page also has an email contact.
